question: Before implementing — has the design been reviewed for the obvious failure modes?
whyHelp:
Here is why this matters right now:
Architecture decisions are the expensive ones to reverse later.
A short design pass now — data flow, boundaries, failure modes — pays for itself.

L1.title: Document the key architectural decisions and trade-offs
L1.body: For each major design decision in the current architecture, state what you chose, what you rejected, and why. Include the constraints that shaped the decision — latency, throughput, deployment environment, operational complexity ceiling. Trade-off documentation now prevents expensive reversals once the system is load-bearing.

L2.title: Document the trade-offs
L2.body: Document the key architecture decisions: what you chose, what you rejected, why, and against which constraints. Prevents costly reversals later.

L3.title: Chosen vs rejected, and why
L3.body: Write down your architecture trade-offs: chosen vs rejected, and why.
